children: an innovative cellular immunotherapy company advancing engineered T cell therapeutics designed to engage phagocytic mechanisms, today announced that the University of California, Davis (UC Davis), has been activated as a clinical trial site for CERTAIN-T, the Company's ongoing Phase 1 study evaluating CER-1236 in patients with hematologic malignancies. UC Davis also serves as the primary manufacturing site for CER-1236.
The activation of UC Davis is expected to expand patient recruitment capacity while leveraging the site's existing manufacturing capabilities to streamline treatment logistics.

Brian Jonas, M.D., Professor, clinician-scientist, and Chief of the Division of Malignant Hematology, Cellular Therapy and Transplantation in the Department of Internal Medicine at the UC Davis School of Medicine and UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center and study investigator on the trial, commented, “We are excited to join with CERo Therapeutics to open this important clinical trial. We look forward to being able to offer a novel and innovative chimeric engulfment receptor-based treatment option for our patients with myeloid malignancies.”

Chris Ehrlich, CERo Therapeutics CEO added, "The addition of UC Davis represents another important milestone in our collaboration, expanding our longstanding relationship beyond manufacturing to include patient enrollment in the CERTAIN-T study. Integrating manufacturing and clinical operations at a single institution has the potential to expand patient access while shortening the time between cell manufacturing and patient infusion. We have been encouraged by the interest we've received from investigators and institutions evaluating participation in the CERTAIN-T trial, and we are pleased to welcome the UC Davis team."

CERo previously reported findings from six patients treated in the first two cohorts of CERTAIN-T. All three patients in the second cohort completed the 28-day dose-limiting toxicity assessment without a DLT. In its June 2026 update, the Company reported that the observed safety profile remained consistent with earlier findings of no cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, DLTs or treatment-related severe adverse events during the DLT assessment window. Preliminary investigator observations noted clinical improvement in two patients; however, formal response assessments remain ongoing, are based on a limited number of patients, and no definitive safety or efficacy conclusions can be drawn at this time. One patient with refractory AML subsequently underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation 71 days after CER-1236 infusion. The study protocol has been amended to include MDS and myelofibrosis.

The first-in-human, multicenter, open-label Phase 1/1b CERTAIN-T study is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary clinical activity of CER-1236 in patients with hematologic malignancies. The study initially enrolled patients with acute myeloid leukemia (“AML”), including relapsed/refractory AML, AML with measurable residual disease (MRD), and newly diagnosed TP53-mutated AML, and the protocol has since been amended to include transfusion-dependent myelodysplastic syndromes (“TD-MDS”), high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (“HR-MDS”), and post-JAK inhibitor myelofibrosis (“MF”). Primary endpoints include safety and tolerability. Secondary endpoints include pharmacokinetics and measures of clinical response, including overall response rate (“ORR”), complete response (“CR”), composite complete response (“cCR”), and measurable residual disease (“MRD”).

CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. is an innovative immunotherapy company advancing the development of engineered T cell therapeutics for the treatment of cancer. The Company’s proprietary approach to T cell engineering is designed to integrate characteristics of innate and adaptive immunity into a single therapeutic construct intended to engage multiple immune mechanisms against cancer. CERo refers to these engineered cells as Chimeric Engulfment Receptor T cells (“CER-T”).
The Company’s lead investigational product candidate, CER-1236, is being evaluated in hematologic malignancies.
